summary: Two summit lookouts on Thunder Mountain, a 1926 cupola cabin and a 1934 50-foot tower, both gone by the 1950s; footings remain; wilderness hike.

facts.design: Cupola cabin (1926) at the south summit and a 50-foot wooden L-4 tower (1934) at the north summit
facts.status_note: Both lookouts were removed or destroyed in the 1950s; footings remain at the north summit.

access.note: In the Salmo-Priest Wilderness and reached only on foot; an old, unmaintained trail leads to the summit from the Shedroof Divide, and the south-slope spur is abandoned.

visit.trail_note: 14 miles round trip from the Thunder Creek trailhead, 2,400 ft of gain. The spur up the south slope is abandoned and not maintained or signed.

events.note: Cupola cabin at the south summit
Mark Cook; cabin struck by lightning, minor burns
50-foot wooden L-4 tower at the north summit; the register says it replaced the cabin, Willhite says both stood until the 1950s
Former Fire Lookout Sites register, US 1531

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's wording says the 1934 tower replaced the 1926 cabin, but the same register entry and Willhite say both stood together until the 1950s. The story follows the coexistence account.
The register and Willhite say the structures were removed in the 1950s; FirelookOut says destroyed in the 1950s. All three agree on the decade, so the story reports both words.

notes_for_editor: Removal is only dated to the 1950s, so there is no removal event and the cabin's destruction a few years after 1926 has no year. The register's replaced wording conflicts with its own coexistence sentence. Willhite's photo captions are undated, so today's footings are as of an unknown visit. The WTA line 'long gone' refers to Shedroof Mountain, not Thunder, and was not used. Only Willhite names a lookout. No reusable photos with licence were found.
